newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends up but outright volume subdued.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends up but outright volume subdued.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures ended higher, but some traders remained sceptical of the rise to three week highs because outright volume remained sluggish.
May closed 10 stg higher at 1,033 stg per tonne, and July jumped 11 to 1,054. Total volume was a healthy 13,147 contracts, but traders said most of that came from crosses.
In the morning, 1,000 December 1997/May 1998 switches traded at 20 and another thousand at 21. Volume in December 1997 stood at 2,472 contracts and May 1998 at 2,608.
May/July spreads were also active as traders rolled forward May positions before first tender day on May 1. July was most active, grabbing 4,085 trades. The May/July spread closed up two at 21.
Light trade buying also helped lift prices, traders said.

Technically, traders said July looked constructive after breaking and holding gains above resistance at 1,046. Though July came within a stg of matching the April 3 and 4 high at 1,062, technical traders remained optimistic.
They expected July to hurdle 1,062 next week and go for the April 2 high of 1,065 to draw in fund buying.

But others who were less optimistic noted that New York has consistently failed to confirm London's upmove. Though CSCE July gapped higher at the open and to fill some of the gap left from the April 7 high of $1,480 and the previous session's low of $1,521, traders said New York quickly ran out of steam and eased off its high.
That slip dragged July here down to a fresh session low and fill a one-stg gap from this morning.
Some traders also worried about lack of outright volume and noted little fund and industry purchases adding to gains.
A lack of concrete fundamentals to support the move also worried traders, though speculation has circulated that Ivory Coast shippers were having trouble finding enough cocoa to fulfill committments.
That helped July and September keep their premiums over December. At the close, July was 19 stg and September 30 stg above December.
But the Ivory Coast is expected to report export figures within the next two weeks, which should more clearly define cocoa's direction.
Until then, skeptics said cocoa's gains could be vulnerable in the near-term. They pegged July support near 1,000, with stronger support at the April 9 low of 980.
In options, no July contracts traded.
